Getting started with pollinatoR

Source: vignettes/pollinatoR.Rmd
pollinatoR.Rmd
library(pollinatoR)

What the package does

pollinatoR estimates how much of a crop’s yield depends on insect pollinators, from experiments that compare plants with and without pollinator access: caged or bagged plants against open ones, and, where a trial has it, a hand-supplemented arm. The methods apply to any crop studied with such a design.

An analysis is built in layers. Each layer is one function that returns an object you can print and check before going on.

Layer Function What you declare or get
Data pollin_data() Which columns are responses, treatment, units, groups and exposures
Design pollin_design() Which treatment level is which arm, and the layout of the experiment
Estimand pollin_estimand() The contrast, the scale and the basis of the number you want
Fit pollin_fit() One mixed model per response
Effects pollin_effects() The estimate with its interval, on the declared scale
Guards pollin_guard_*() Checks against common errors of analysis and reading

A simulated study

Twelve sites, sixteen plants per site, half caged and half open. Two yield components are recorded per plant, along with counts of honey bees and other insects. Open access raises pod count by an amount that varies between sites, and slightly more on plants with more honey bees.

set.seed(1)
n_site <- 12L
n_plant <- 16L
site <- rep(sprintf("s%02d", seq_len(n_site)), each = n_plant)
trt <- rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = n_plant / 2L), n_site)
honeybee <- rep(rpois(n_site, 8), each = n_plant) + rpois(n_site * n_plant, 1)
wild <- rep(rpois(n_site, 4), each = n_plant) + rpois(n_site * n_plant, 1)
idx <- as.integer(factor(site))
site_effect <- rnorm(n_site, 0, 0.3)[idx]
site_slope <- rnorm(n_site, 0, 0.25)[idx]
open <- trt == "Open"
pod_mu <- exp(1.8 + site_effect + (0.35 + site_slope + 0.015 * honeybee) * open)
seed_mu <- exp(2.6 + site_effect + (0.12 + site_slope / 2) * open)
pods <- rnbinom(n_site * n_plant, mu = pod_mu, size = 15)
seeds_per_pod <- rnbinom(n_site * n_plant, mu = seed_mu, size = 15)
canola <- data.frame(site, trt, honeybee, wild, pods, seeds_per_pod)
head(canola)
#>   site  trt honeybee wild pods seeds_per_pod
#> 1  s01 Cage        7    3    3             9
#> 2  s01 Cage        7    5    0             4
#> 3  s01 Cage        8    5    4             1
#> 4  s01 Cage        7    2    2             4
#> 5  s01 Cage        7    2    4             6
#> 6  s01 Cage       10    2    2             7

Data

pollin_data() pairs the table with a map of what each column is. The roles are checked against the data, and the structural checks of pollin_validate() are run and stored.

pd <- pollin_data(
  canola,
  response = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  unit = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild")
)
pd
#> <pollin_data>
#>   rows        : 192 
#>   response    : pods, seeds_per_pod 
#>   treatment   : trt ( Cage, Open )
#>   unit        : site 
#>   exposures   : honeybee, wild 
#>   checks      : 0 warnings; see `$checks`

Design

pollin_design() says which treatment level is the excluded arm and which is the open arm, and names the layout. The layout sets the random structure of the models: here each site carries a random intercept and a random treatment slope, so the pollinator effect may differ between sites.

ds <- pollin_design(
  pd,
  arms = c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"),
  layout = "multi_site"
)
ds
#> <pollin_design>
#>   layout    : multi_site 
#>   arms      : excluded = Cage, open = Open 
#>   reference : open 
#>   units     : site 
#>   random    : (trt | site)

The five layouts are crd, rcbd, split_plot, matched_pairs and multi_site; ?pollin_design gives the random structure each one implies. A random treatment slope needs enough sites to estimate its variance; with only a handful of sites, slope = FALSE in pollin_design() fits a random intercept alone.

Estimand

pollin_estimand() names the number the analysis is for. The dependence (E2) compares excluded plants with the reference arm; the deficit (E1), available when a trial has a supplemented arm, compares supplemented with open plants. The scale is one of "difference", "ratio", "rii" or "lnrr".

The basis has no default. A loss share, 1−E[Yexcl]/E[Yopen]1 - E[Y_\mathrm{excl}]/E[Y_\mathrm{open}], is the part of the present yield that pollinators supply. A gain, E[Yopen]/E[Yexcl]−1E[Y_\mathrm{open}]/E[Y_\mathrm{excl}] - 1, is the rise over a crop without them. Excluded plants yielding 75% of open ones give a loss share of 25% and a gain of 33%. They answer different questions, and the package records which one every result is.

est <- pollin_estimand(ds, family = "dependence", scale = "ratio", basis = "loss")
est
#> <pollin_estimand>
#>   family     : dependence (E2) 
#>   contrast   : Open vs Cage 
#>   scale      : ratio 
#>   basis      : loss 
#>   population : trial 
#>   layout     : multi_site 
#>   assumptions: 6 ; see `pollin_assumptions()`
knitr::kable(pollin_assumptions(est))
assumption statement
consistency Each arm is one well-defined treatment, applied the same way on every unit.
excludability The exclusion device changes the response only by excluding pollinators (no cage effect on microclimate, pests or handling).
no_interference One unit’s treatment does not change another unit’s response, for example by displacing pollinators to neighbouring units.
assignment Arms were randomised within each site; the contrast is read within sites.
positive_means The expected response is positive in both arms, so the ratio is defined.
population The estimand refers to the units in the trial; carrying it to other fields or seasons is a further assumption.

The assumptions are statements about the experiment that the data cannot confirm. They belong in the methods section of any report.

Fit and effects

pollin_fit() fits one glmmTMB model per response, with the treatment as the fixed effect and the design’s random terms. The family is chosen from each response’s values unless supplied.

fit <- pollin_fit(est)
fit
#> <pollin_fit>
#>   engine    : glmmTMB 
#>   family    : dependence 
#>   contrast  : Open vs Cage 
#>   model     : <response> ~ trt + (trt | site) 
#>   pods      : nbinom2, 192 rows
#>   seeds_per_pod: nbinom2, 192 rows

pollin_effects() reads the contrast from each model: every plant is predicted under each arm, the predictions are averaged, and the scale is applied to the two averages. A ratio-type estimate is a ratio of averaged predictions, not an average of plant-level ratios.

eff <- pollin_effects(fit)
eff
#> <pollin_effects>
#>   family   : dependence (E2) 
#>   scale    : ratio 
#>   basis    : loss 
#>   estimate : 1 - Cage/Open (loss share) 
#>   interval : 95% delta 
#>   note     : delta intervals cover fixed-effect uncertainty only
#>       response     contrast    estimate  std.error   conf.low conf.high
#>           pods Open vs Cage 0.360830947 0.05885434  0.2344141 0.4663733
#>  seeds_per_pod Open vs Cage 0.001935728 0.06804443 -0.1407497 0.1267740
#>       p.value     family scale basis distribution interval
#>  1.168706e-06 dependence ratio  loss      nbinom2    delta
#>  9.773268e-01 dependence ratio  loss      nbinom2    delta

A parametric bootstrap interval is available with interval = "bootstrap"; A three-arm trial: deficit and dependence shows it.

For the contribution on the difference scale, with a false discovery rate adjustment across responses and the standard deviation of the site-level treatment slope, pollin_contribution() wraps the fit and the effects.

est_diff <- pollin_estimand(
  ds,
  family = "dependence",
  scale = "difference",
  basis = "loss"
)
contribution <- pollin_contribution(est_diff)
contribution$table[
  c("response", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "slope_sd", "p.fdr")
]
#>        response   estimate  conf.low conf.high  slope_sd        p.fdr
#> 1          pods 3.70932785  2.139484  5.279172 0.2170980 7.273592e-06
#> 2 seeds_per_pod 0.02967876 -2.015275  2.074632 0.1327942 9.773070e-01

Which insects drive the effect

pollin_moderation() fits treatment-by-exposure interactions, with each exposure split into a between-site part (the site mean) and a within-site part (the deviation from it). The within-site interaction is estimated from variation inside a site, where anything constant at site level, such as an unrecorded variety, is held fixed.

pollin_moderation(ds, outcome = "pods")
#> <pollin_moderation>  outcome: pods  (treatment x exposure)
#>                      term    estimate  std.error   p.value            component
#>   trtOpen:honeybee_within -0.06756023 0.06933630 0.3298656      within (robust)
#>  trtOpen:honeybee_between  0.02280788 0.09032579 0.8006493 between (vulnerable)
#>       trtOpen:wild_within  0.01511041 0.06998086 0.8290485      within (robust)
#>      trtOpen:wild_between  0.03201095 0.09144191 0.7262872 between (vulnerable)
#>      p.fdr
#>  0.6597312
#>         NA
#>  0.8290485
#>         NA

Within a site, honey bee counts here differ by only a bee or two between plants, too little for this small trial to separate the planted effect from zero. The within-site terms are the ones to read; the between-site terms carry whatever differs between sites along with the insects.

The split itself is pollin_within_between().

wb <- pollin_within_between(canola$honeybee, group = canola$site)
head(as.data.frame(wb))
#>    within between
#> 1 -0.1875  7.1875
#> 2 -0.1875  7.1875
#> 3  0.8125  7.1875
#> 4 -0.1875  7.1875
#> 5 -0.1875  7.1875
#> 6  2.8125  7.1875

Guards

Guards stop or warn on common analysis errors. pollin_guard_spurious() tests the regression of a dependence index on open-arm yield across units. The open-arm value sits on both axes, so part of any slope is built in. The guard permutes the excluded arm while holding the open arm fixed and compares the observed slope with that null.

open_mean <- tapply(canola$pods[open], canola$site[open], mean)
cage_mean <- tapply(canola$pods[!open], canola$site[!open], mean)
pollin_guard_spurious(open_mean, cage_mean, n_perm = 200, seed = 1)
#> <pollin_spurious>  index ~ open-yield slope guard
#>   observed slope : 0.0137
#>   coupling null  : mean 0.0528, sd 0.0164 (n_perm = 200)
#>   permutation p  : 1.000  -> slope consistent with mechanical coupling (SPURIOUS risk)

pollin_guard_bounded() refuses to average site-level ratios unless asked, because the mean of ratios is not the ratio of means.

try(pollin_guard_bounded(ds, index = "rii", response = "pods"))
#> Error : Averaging bounded per-unit ratios is not the ratio of expected values; the mean of 12 unit-level RII values is not the trial's RII. The RII of the arm means is 0.2194. Set `allow = TRUE` to average them anyway.

The other two guards are pollin_guard_ecological(), which warns when an exposure slope exists only between units, and pollin_guard_posttreatment(), which refuses an adjustment covariate declared to be affected by the treatment. Both are shown in A matched-pair field study.

Descriptive indices

pollin_index() and pollin_rii() give the Relative Interaction Index, the log response ratio and the dependence ratio from unit-level arm means, with intervals where one is available. They are for comparison with published work; the model-based estimate above is the primary one.

pollin_index(ds, response = "pods", n_boot = 500, seed = 1)
#>              index  estimate  conf.low conf.high
#> 1              RII 0.2194222 0.1003973 0.3440582
#> 2             lnRR 0.4460981 0.1599727 0.7322235
#> 3 dependence_ratio 0.3598790        NA        NA
#>                                                              note
#> 1                                                    bootstrap CI
#> 2                                                  closed-form CI
#> 3 point; do not regress on open yield (see pollin_guard_spurious)

pollin_compensation() summarises how the yield components trade off against each other across plants.

pollin_compensation(pd)
#> <pollin_compensation>  ( spearman correlations )
#>              a    b       cor compensation
#>  seeds_per_pod pods 0.4296379        FALSE
#>   0 negatively-correlated pairs -> candidate compensation

Checking the data

pollin_validate() reports missing values in declared columns, expected factor levels and any identities supplied, as counts only.

pollin_validate(pd, expect_levels = list(trt = c("Cage", "Open")))
#> <pollin_validate>
#>       check status    detail
#>        rows   INFO       192
#>        cols   INFO         6
#>  levels:trt   PASS Cage,Open

Moving from pollin_spec()

pollin_spec() was removed at version 0.2.0. It declared the data and the design in one call; they are now two layers.

# Before
spec <- pollin_spec(
  canola,
  outcomes = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  control = "Cage",
  random = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild"),
  latent_unit = "site"
)
pollin_contribution(spec)
pollin_moderation(spec, outcome = "pods")
# Now
pd <- pollin_data(
  canola,
  response = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  unit = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild")
)
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "multi_site")
pollin_contribution(pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "difference", basis = "loss"))
pollin_moderation(ds, outcome = "pods")

outcomes becomes response, random becomes unit, control becomes the excluded entry of arms, and latent_unit becomes the slope argument of pollin_design() (the multi_site layout puts the slope on the site by default).
